> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 47 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8e505db8178cedbed174049b211cc409b22adaea` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da402338d742a106576c146871270878dd8fe707` — the merge of head `b99d86a144ed9c23d9170c5802a2f27ac480dd90` into base `8e505db8178cedbed174049b211cc409b22adaea`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da402338d742a106576c146871270878dd8fe707 && git checkout da402338d742a106576c146871270878dd8fe707
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8e505db8178cedbed174049b211cc409b22adaea b99d86a144ed9c23d9170c5802a2f27ac480dd90 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8e505db8178cedbed174049b211cc409b22adaea && git merge --no-ff b99d86a144ed9c23d9170c5802a2f27ac480dd90

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8e505db8178cedbed174049b211cc409b22adaea
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8e505db8178cedbed174049b211cc409b22adaea` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ecf1fd4a39fb1e0b188e276bfa3ba14c62eea2e7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts (`namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal`, `namedBaseCloseSubject`, `closedOverlayWriteClauses`, `NamedBaseWriteOperation`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the save, per-item publish, `publishPackageDrafts` / `promoteDraftForPublish`, rollback and delete doors), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts (the census and move, #29392), packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/packageless-overlays.ts (`reasonOf`, `jsonRow`, the preview listing), .changeset/28905-named-base-overlay-write-closed.md (the #28905 Now refused / Still open lists), card #29390's live state (ruling 6579511992). Read on `origin/main` `390bd2ae`; the PR's own changeset is prose outside `hits` and is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #29393 body and all five comments (triage 6582524180, claim 6583771832, reports 6584466731 and 6585010191, claim amendment 6584492790); PR #29535 body, file list (2 files, +50/-19) and the net diff against `main` at the head; the 63 check-runs on the head. The PR body was written at 6b1ea514 and is stale on the `replacement` (it says untouched; the tree edits it under the amendment) — judged on the tree, as the brief says.

Check-runs on `ecf1fd4a`: 63 total — 53 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in and conditional jobs: 18.x upgrade harness, packed-tarball smoke, Build Docs, Lint UI, UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the dogfood matrix shell, the schedule gate), 1 `in_progress` (Test Core 6/8) at review time. Every concluded gate is green, including Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, the Lint and Type Check families and Test Core 1-5, 7, 8. Judged on what has concluded; the one running shard is named, not assumed.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept set moves: the diff edits the string fields `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` of one exported `SemanticMigration` object and adds a changeset. No schema, no runtime code, no export name, no test. Right.
- Public surface implied: the text of a `@objectstack/spec` export (`MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic`'s entry) and what is generated from it at PR time and at publish — the protocol upgrade guide section for this hop and `spec-changes.json`. The entry is unreleased (`packages/spec` is at 18.2.0; its CHANGELOG does not carry `packageless-overlay-write-closed`; the id appears only in the entry and two pending changesets), so no released guide text changes under a reader. Right.
- The widening keeps the #29457 wording (1896e313): clause (1) of the new `surface` is the previous surface re-cut as a numbered address, with "one installed read-only package ships" and the own-member exception intact; the `reason` and `replacement` sentences #29457 wrote are kept verbatim. Right.
- The card's conditional line (a "commit revert stays open" sentence if #29390 ruled so): #29390 is open with no PR, and its seat ruling 6579511992 is fork A (the restore limb of `revertCommit` / `rollbackToPackageCommit` is to be closed with the same sentence). No line added — right. On `main` today that path is still open and the entry does not name it, which is accurate to the tree; when #29390 lands, its own ADR-0087 disposition decides whether address (2) gains the commit revert (the dev's out_of_scope carrier, correctly not filed here).
- Docs Drift Check lists 12 hand-written pages via the new path literal `/api/v1/packages/BASE/publish-drafts` in `surface`. The entry names that route only as a closed write address; nothing on those pages becomes false. No action.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29393-overlay-write-entry-both-addresses.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `Clause-②: no (migration entry prose; no accept set moves)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Matches the diff: prose of an exported object in one package, no narrowing arm, no `!` title, no BREAKING banner. The parenthetical after `no` is ordinary reasoning, not an arm (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s own control at its line 3743 reads exactly this shape as a plain `no`); Check Changeset concluded `success` on the head. No ADR-0087 marker is owed: the marker is required of a breaking change, and this is neither breaking nor a registration (the registration marker lives on `28576-packageless-overlay-write-closed.md`, and #28905's changeset already records `not-required (already-registered packageless-overlay-write-closed)` naming this very widening as the `packages/spec` edit it did not make). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. Clause-②: `no` — right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (report 6584466731): the `replacement` did not fit rows bound to the base (the `foreign_declaration` remedy, and "every row ... keeps its package-less write"). Answered A by claim amendment 6584492790 (seat widened the file surface to the `replacement` text, same PR); implemented in `ecf1fd4a`; report 6585010191 lists no open question. Closed.
- Claim surface: two files, both inside the amended claim. `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (frozen by server seat 5 until 06:00Z) is untouched. Held.
- Dev deviations: the model-free commit trailer pair per AGENTS.md (a repo rule, not a review matter); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally — covered by CI (Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Lint families all `success`). Closed.
- `body_amendments`: the dev names four stale places in the PR body (the `replacement` bullet, the acceptance-notes bullet now done, the test head, the gate counts) and asks the seat to write them. Not a tree defect; the seat owes the body edit before merge so the record of what landed is not contradicted by the PR's own account. Escalated to the seat, no verdict weight.
- Out-of-scope carrier (#29390's revert close and the entry's address (2)): noted on the card, correctly left to that card.

### ④ Design judgment

`18.packageless-overlay-write-closed.ts`, judged against the code it cites on `main` and the scenario it is accepted against (an operator reading the generated 18.x upgrade guide after both closes shipped).

**`surface` — address (2) against `namedBaseCloseSubject` and the doors.** Holds, clause for clause. The doors that ask the named-base close on `main`: the save door (`protocol.ts` ~15721, `request.source === undefined`, draft or active — "a save in draft or publish mode"); `promoteDraftForPublish` (~18613, judged on `promoteInto`, before `repo.promoteDraft`), reached from `publishMetaItemUnaudited` (18166, the per-item `POST /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME/publish?package=BASE`) and from `publishPackageDrafts` (19786, `POST /api/v1/packages/BASE/publish-drafts`) — "a per-item publish ... publish-drafts holding such a draft"; the rollback door (~22820, on `resolveOverlayPackageBinding`'s answer, i.e. the row's own binding — "a rollback of a row bound to the package"). The delete door asks only the package-less close (~23466) and `NamedBaseWriteOperation` excludes `delete` — "(a delete naming the package keeps the write)" holds, and `protocol.named-base-overlay-write.test.ts:272` pins it. The conditions "where the pair can be ensured, the base records a version and the override write gate admits the declared body into the pair" are `namedBaseCloseSubject`'s four exits (pair id forms, `customizationPairEnsureRefusal` undefined, `manifest.version` a non-empty string, `overrideWriteVerdict` not `refuse`) in the words of the #28905 changeset's Now refused list. The stored-rows clause ("package-less or bound to the read-only package itself") matches the census population since #29392. One omission is harmless: a body already carrying `overrides` is not this close's (the D2 gate's), which the entry need not say.

**`reason` against the refusal text and the open doors.** Holds. "a row bound to that package, declaring nothing, served in place of the package's own document" is the `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal` docblock; "refused 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE naming the pair and the `overrides` declaration" is `closedOverlayWriteClauses` (`pair` with its `?package=` address, `declared` = `overrides: { package, basedOn }`) under `closedOverlayWriteError` (code `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, status 403); "a delete naming the package stays open, as the way to remove such a row, and so does every write the pair could not take, an email template locale the base does not ship among them" is the Still open list and the `NamedBaseWriteOperation` docblock. The sentence "The close reaches only what the command moves as a declared override" still scopes the package-less close only, which is what it says.

**`replacement` against the cli and the census.** Holds. "the preview names \"bound to\" that package and `--json` marks `boundToBase`" — `packageless-overlays.ts` line 392 prints `bound to ${row.base}` on a movable row and `jsonRow` emits `boundToBase: true`. The bound `foreign_declaration` remedy ("delete it naming the package, then save its body into the pair, declaring `overrides: { package: BASE, basedOn }`") is `reasonOf`'s `boundToBase` arm word for word, and its premise ("a save naming the package is closed") is right: the save that would strip the key carries no `overrides`, so `namedBaseCloseSubject` judges it and closes it where the pair can take it. The `multi_shipped` clause, which still prescribes a delete naming no package, is correct as scoped: the census classifies a bound row by its binding as the one shipper, so a bound row is never `multi_shipped` (module header, "the rows bound to a read-only base"). The `shadowed` and `no_pair` clauses apply to both bindings unchanged. "every bound row it lists and does not move keeps its delete naming the package" is true of every bound disposition. The own-member exception reaches bound rows too (`addedMemberOf` runs for any movable row); the move deletes a bound row by its own binding (`packageId: bound ? row.base : null`), so "moves ... into the base's paired .custom" is one description for both.

**Tried to break it; what held and what did not.**

- Could the entry prescribe a step the doors refuse? No: every remedy it names is either into the pair (`?package=BASE.custom`, open), a delete (open at both addresses where the ceremony does not move the row), or the ceremony itself.
- Could an operator following it lose a customization? No: the bound remedy deletes only after the body is to be saved into the pair, in the order the cli prints, and the `shadowed` way out is the pair DELETE the entry already names.
- Could the guide render break? The surface carries backticks and double quotes; the generator fences the code span by longest backtick run (`upgrade-guide-surface-span.test.ts` round-trips every real entry) and the dev's `check:upgrade-guide` run plus the green Test Core shards cover it. No pipe is introduced. Holds.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix, text the guide prints).** Line 49 of the head file: `'packages ship the name):delete it naming no package, ...'` — the space after the colon was dropped in this diff (`main` reads `name): delete`). It renders as `name):delete` in the generated upgrade guide. One-character fix in the same string.
- **S2 (should-fix, in the `hits` file).** The header comment (lines 5-12) still describes the entry as "a write naming no package ... is refused" and "the package-less Setup rows those writes made", while the entry now registers both closed addresses and both kinds of stored row. A reader of the file (and the next card on it) is told half the entry. Two sentences in the comment; the PR body calls it out as outside the claimed text, but the claim amendment widened the surface to this file's `replacement`, so the file is the claim and its header should agree with it.
- **S3 (should-fix, precision).** The `failed`-move tail: "the row may also be left, as it keeps its package-less write (a bound row, its delete naming the package)". For exactly the two failure causes that sentence names (the pair cannot be ensured; the base records no version), `namedBaseCloseSubject` returns `null`, so a bound row keeps its save naming the package as well, not only its delete — which the entry's own `reason` says ("so does every write the pair could not take"). True as written, narrower than the code; "(a bound row, its delete naming the package, and the save naming it where the pair could not take the override)" closes the gap.
- Observation, no finding: `acceptanceCriteria` still names only the package-less control (the save naming no package answers 403); a parallel control naming the base would pin address (2), but the criterion as written is still a true and sufficient acceptance.

No must-fix. The three should-fixes are one-line text edits in the same file and do not move the verdict.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:spec#3` · head `b99d86a144ed9c23d9170c5802a2f27ac480dd90` · 2026-11-02T19:07Z
